title: Find out whether an exported video looks brighter than the same moment on the canvas
goal: While measuring video fades, the MP4 read back after export came out about a tenth brighter than the canvas at the same moment, faded or not, and a little darker in the darkest frames. Find out whether a person playing the file in QuickTime actually sees a different picture from the editor, or whether it is only how the file was read back.
notes: Seen 2026-10-03 by the measureFade walk step (Scripts/playtest/a-video-clip-fades-walk.json; numbers in queue/audits/2026-10-03-video-fades-measured.json). Command: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/a-video-clip-fades-walk.json --no-build. Output at 3000 ms (no fade): canvas stopped 0.297, export's pre-encode picture (EditorState.stillFrame) 0.299, MP4 via AVAssetImageGenerator 0.328. At 250 ms of a 1s fade: canvas 0.075, pre-encode 0.075, MP4 0.064. So the renderer agrees with the canvas; the difference arrives at encode or at read-back (DocumentMovieWriter writes BGRA sRGB into H.264; generator output drawn into an sRGB context for Rec.709 luma). NOT reproduced as something a person sees: only measured through AVAssetImageGenerator. Could be untagged/limited-range read-back rather than the file.
acceptance: The exported MP4 and the canvas are compared at the same moment in a real player (QuickTime) and the answer is written down with pictures
If they differ visibly, a p1 task names the cause (colour space, video range, transfer curve) and the fix; if not, this task records why the read-back differed and is closed

log.note: Reproduced in real QuickTime (probe --capture-diag screenshots, unlocked screen): untagged export plays sRGB 76 as 86, 128 as 139, 16 as 14; red (255,0,0) as (231,23,0). Cause: the movie writer sets no colour properties, file is untagged (ffprobe on a real 1080p probe export), VideoToolbox guesses SMPTE-C/601/709 transfer. Tagging 709 primaries + sRGB transfer + 709 matrix round-trips exactly; 709 transfer alone does not. Write-up with pictures: docs/progress/2026-10-04-export-brightness.md. Fix filed p1: an-exported-video-plays-with-the-same-brightness.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Yes, it looks different: in real QuickTime an exported MP4 plays mid greys lighter (sRGB 76 as 86), deepest greys darker and reds/greens shifted, because the movie writer leaves the file untagged and players guess SMPTE-C/601/709. Pictures and numbers in docs/progress/2026-10-04-export-brightness.md; fix (tag 709 primaries + sRGB transfer + 709 matrix, verified to round-trip) filed as p1 an-exported-video-plays-with-the-same-brightness.
